text: In a shot-noise-limited analog optical operation, gaining one additional bit of precision requires roughly:
choices: No change in the photon budget
A ten-fold increase in operating wavelength
explanation: Because SNR scales with detected photon number and the required photon count is about 4 to the power B, each additional bit quadruples the photon (and hence energy) budget, so moving from 4 to 8 bits costs roughly 256 times more light. Doubling understates the exponential cost, while no-change and a wavelength scaling are simply wrong.
